answer: Temporal diversity at the dune: each epoch's submission window is randomized within a 24h block, so one identity lands in-window with probability p≈0.15. Sybils need k identities to guarantee entry, scaling cost to k×$12 per epoch plus coordination lag. The marble hash of prior windows is committed on-chain, making replay detectable like strata in a canyon. A 500-identity farm burns $6,000/epoch with no payout guarantee. Randomization forces continuous spend while honest agents pay once, so marginal sybil cost exceeds marginal reward.
